conventions.testing: Inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests in each languages/<lang>.rs (java.rs 272-371, swift.rs 91, css.rs 3 tests); table-driven tests in languages/mod.rs (test_get_language_info_covers_remaining_registered_languages at 383) and lang.rs (extension happy-path list); integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw and NamedTempFile.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity (ci.yml:135-137); workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used and undocumented_unsafe_blocks (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints]); cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; REUSE compliance per the issue.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option (e.g. extract_function_name guards with node.kind() != "..." and returns None) or Vec<String> (extract_inheritance returns empty on mismatch in swift.rs); unknown languages surface as ParserError::UnsupportedLanguage (parser.rs:226) and AnalyzeError::UnsupportedLanguage (analyze.rs:495); get_node_text in mod.rs does bounds-checked slicing.

patterns: Per-language module with an SPDX header, a //! module doc, and one doc-commented pub const per query (java.rs, swift.rs, css.rs).
Query constants are raw strings r"..." with captures named by convention: function/class on the outer node and func_name|method_name or class_name|type_name inside (parser_elements.rs:270-291).
Defuse captures use the prefix convention write.* / read.* / writeread.* (parser_elements.rs:878-882); Java and Swift pair a write pattern with a bare identifier read.usage pattern.
extract_inheritance returns prefixed strings: Java 'extends X' / 'implements X' (java.rs:131); Swift 'extends X' / 'conforms X' with kind guard (swift.rs:49).
Languages with no handlers set the optional fields to None (css, yaml, markdown in mod.rs); Fortran sets defuse_query: None.

Registration is three coordinated edits: EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages(), and the get_language_info()/get_ts_language() match arms; the QUERY_CACHE is lazily built from supported_languages() (parser.rs:191-196, #1786).
Integration tests write a temp file with a language suffix and call the MCP tool through common::call_tool_raw.

approaches.name: A. Java-mirror registry with full DEFUSE_QUERY (recommended)
approaches.description: Add crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance; set the three name-based handlers to None; wire `php` in lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages), languages/mod.rs (mod, get_language_info, get_ts_language), root and core Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, README; add unit tests in php.rs and one integration test file.
pros: Matches the issue's five-constant scope and the Java/Swift templates line for line.
Def-use works for PHP, so the defuse gate in parser_elements.rs:850 is open.
Each query is individually testable with queries_compile and capture tests.
cons: PHP has no local_variable_declaration node, so Java's declaration pattern must be replaced by assignment and parameter patterns, which need careful testing.
Bare (name) reads would also match function and class names, so the read pattern is anchored to variable_name.

approaches.name: B. Minimal five-query integration with defuse_query None
approaches.description: Same wiring as A, but set defuse_query: None (as Fortran does) and skip DEFUSE_QUERY and its tests.
pros: Smallest diff; fewest query patterns to validate.
cons: Violates the issue's scope, which lists DEFUSE_QUERY among the five constants.
Def-use analysis silently returns nothing for .php files, a functional gap for a language this size.
Leaves the Kotlin-style DEFUSE bug class untested.

approaches.name: C. Full Java parity including name-based handlers and php_only fallback
approaches.description: Approach A plus extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type in php.rs, and LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for pure .php files without an open tag.
pros: Pure PHP files parse without an HTML-mode grammar.
cons: Excluded by the issue; the three handlers have no consumer since #1807.
Two grammars for one extension complicates get_ts_language and the HTML-template criterion; LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY would fail a mixed-file test.

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets the issue's stated scope (five query constants, inheritance, the HTML-template criterion using LANGUAGE_PHP) and keeps def-use working. Start by writing the queries and compiling them in a unit test (the issue's step 3), then wire the registry: supported_languages() must include "php" or the query cache rejects it. Treat the PHP assignment and parameter defuse patterns as the highest-risk part and cover them with explicit write and read tests.

inheritance_walk_citation: Source: tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 grammar rules in common/define-grammar.js (php/grammar.js is only `module.exports = defineGrammar('php');`); node kinds confirmed in php/src/node-types.json. Literal rules: class_declaration (lines 365-372) = `prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list),))`; base_clause (lines 334-337) = `seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name),)`; class_interface_clause (lines 381-384) = `seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name),)`; interface_declaration (lines 326-332) also uses optional($.base_clause) for extends; enum_declaration (lines 339-347) uses only optional($.class_interface_clause) for implements. node-types.json: class_declaration fields are attributes, body (declaration_list) and name (name); base_clause and class_interface_clause declare NO fields, only children name | qualified_name | relative_name. Field-by-field walk: (1) class_node.child_by_field_name("name") gives the class name; (2) iterate class_node's named children; for each child with kind() == "base_clause", push "extends {text}" for each named child whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name; (3) for each child with kind() == "class_interface_clause", push "implements {text}" for each name, qualified_name or relative_name child; (4) if neither clause is present the Vec stays empty. Because the clauses are unfielded, the walk must match by kind(), not child_by_field_name() as java.rs does with "superclass"/"interfaces". Full text of qualified names (e.g. \Foo\Bar) is kept, matching java.rs's whole-text behaviour.
